questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that I wanted to go to the US during my bachelors and wanted a "real American travel experience". I narrowed down my search to good schools in the US and since one of my best friends went to UW and loved it the choice was easy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I absolutely loved studying abroad. I made really good friends in the US and had interesting courses. I am not giving a score of 10 since one of the courses was really bad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy since UW made an effort to be welcoming towards incoming students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to a campus tour and received my bus pass and student ID upon arrival. Other than that I didn't receive that much assistance, but further assistance would have been accessible if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is super hard to find housing in Madison. If you want anything somewhat affordable you have to sign a lease a year prior to arrival. I was very lucky as I have a friend who helped me find cheap housing. A lot of my fellow exchange students ended up paying double the rent they pay in Copenhagen or had to sign one year leases that they could not get rid of after the exchange. I know people who paid 15.000 DKK every month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find your accommodations as soon as you get accepted through KU, not when you get accepted by UW. Be proactive and use Facebook groups and sites for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration itself took a long time, but was fairly easy. The course enrollment was a bit annoying, but mostly because the pre approval by KU took a long time and they changed their decision several times.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to send in your financial statements, transcripts, passport and other administrative stuff. They will tell you if something is missing and will give you a chance to send in any missing documents even after the deadline.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The UW exchange team is really helpful and will answer your question really fast if you send them an email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in getting all of my wanted classes in the end. I was waitlisted for one of them and didn't get in until two weeks before departure from Denmark, which was super stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get your pre approvals as early as possible as the course registration is super competitive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took 3 courses with 4 credits each. 2 of the courses were really good, while one of them had the worst professor I have ever encountered.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one 300 level, which was too easy in comparison to KU. One of the courses was a 400 level, which was easier than KU courses, but I still learned something. The last course was a 500 level and super difficult, it is comparable to the harder courses at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was pretty similar to KU. I had two lectures and one discussion in each course each week and one assignment in each course per week. The biggest difference was that assignments and midterms were graded and one exam was multiple choice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON330 - Money and Banking with Steven Rick
ECON461- International Macroeconomics with Stella Chan
ECON521 - Game theory and economic analysis with Benjamin Bernard

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both ECON461 and ECON521. Both courses have good professors and are really interesting. ECON521 is hard, but you can get it approved as Micro III which is super neat.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: UW has its own insurance policy (SHIP) for International students. It is mandatory and more expensive than if you just had gotten a normal travel insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food prices are comparable to Denmark and sometimes a bit more expensive. Going out to bars is way cheaper than Copenhagen. The books are super expensive, but you can usually find them used or as a pdf online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs available and everyone was encouraged to take part in them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were both language clubs and different academic clubs. The campus gyms are amazing and free for students!! The new gym is huge and has amazing amenities like a swimming pool and an ice rink.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The cheese club is so fun! Also go to the gyms if you like working out. It is also highly recommended to apply to ScanDesign as they help a lot with socializing with other Danes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on a road trip with a close friend of mine before the semester started, which I highly recommend doing! We took the east coast route and went to Michigan, Canada, the Niagara Falls, Boston and New York City. Some of my other friends flew to LA where they bought a car and went all the way down Route 66. If you have time and money I highly encourage a road trip. Things that you can do near Madison are going to Milwaukee or Chicago or walking around the Picnic Point if its just for a day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was super easy. Madison is a really nice city and the culture is not that different to Denmark, so you won't be experiencing a culture shock per se.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met my American friends through ScanDesign, clubs and classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find anything challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kindness. People are so welcoming and it is super easy to build up profound friendships. It is so much easier to make friends in the US than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find accommodation early, sign up for ScanDesign and try to not have any classes on Fridays.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find your classes before the first day of school. The campus is really big and some buildings are confusing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I went to my friends parents house in Michigan for Thanksgiving. We stayed there for a week and I just had the most wonderful time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the work load of homework was a bit high, but I'm also an overachiever, so you will probably be fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
